questions.prompt: When do you actually need to enter your UPI PIN?

options.text: Only when money is leaving your account or checking your own balance
To receive money from a buyer on a marketplace
options.explanationWrong: A UPI PIN is never needed to receive money. Anyone who says it is, is trying to trick you.

options.text: To accept a cashback or prize credit
options.explanationWrong: Real cashbacks credit automatically without entering a PIN.

options.text: Whenever a caller says it is a refund verification
options.explanationWrong: Scammers disguise payment debits as 'refunds'. Never enter a PIN to receive funds.

questions.explanationCorrect: Your UPI PIN only authorises outgoing payments or balance checks inside your own app—never incoming money.

questions.prompt: A marketplace buyer says: 'Tap Approve and enter your PIN to receive the payment.' What should you do?

options.text: Enter the PIN quickly so the buyer does not cancel
options.explanationWrong: Rushing is what the scammer wants. Entering the PIN sends your money out.

options.text: Try with a ₹1 test transfer first
options.explanationWrong: You should never approve a collect request or scan a QR to receive payment.

options.text: Decline the collect request, verify your balance, and block/report the UPI ID
Share the PIN in chat so the buyer can finish it
options.explanationWrong: Never share your PIN with anyone, for any reason.

questions.explanationCorrect: Decline the request without entering your PIN, check your account safely, and block and report the sender.

questions.prompt: What happens when you approve a UPI collect request?

options.text: Money is credited to your bank account
options.explanationWrong: It is the opposite: a collect request asks YOU to pay.

options.text: Money leaves your account once you enter your PIN
It only confirms your registered name to the buyer
options.explanationWrong: Approving a collect request initiates a real debit transaction.

options.text: It pauses all pending alerts for 24 hours
options.explanationWrong: Approving a collect request is a payment prompt, not a notification setting.

questions.explanationCorrect: A collect request asks you to pay. Approving it and entering your PIN debits money from your account.

questions.prompt: A buyer sends a QR code and tells you to scan it to 'receive' ₹5,000 for your sofa. Why is that a trap?

options.text: Scanning a QR code in a UPI app initiates a payment FROM you, not TO you
QR codes only work for bank transfers above ₹1 lakh
options.explanationWrong: QR codes work for any amount, but scanning one makes you the payer.

options.text: QR codes expire after 10 seconds
options.explanationWrong: Expiry is not the issue—the direction of payment is.

options.text: You have to pay a 2% fee when receiving via QR
options.explanationWrong: Receiving UPI money is free and never requires scanning a stranger's QR code.

questions.explanationCorrect: Scanning someone else's QR code always starts an outgoing payment. To receive money, just share your UPI ID or your own QR.

questions.prompt: Before tapping anything on a payment prompt inside your UPI app, what clue confirms you are about to lose money?

options.text: A message saying 'DEBIT' or 'Paying' instead of money credited
The prompt shows the name of your bank
options.explanationWrong: All genuine UPI screens show your linked bank name.

options.text: The prompt arrives during business hours
options.explanationWrong: Time of day does not tell you whether a request is safe.

options.text: The buyer has a regular first name
options.explanationWrong: Scammers use ordinary names and fake business handles.

questions.explanationCorrect: Read the direction carefully: collect requests warn that money will be debited from your account if approved.

questions.prompt: After declining a fake collect request in your UPI app, what is the best next step?

options.text: Call the stranger back to ask why they sent it
options.explanationWrong: Engaging the scammer invites more social engineering.

options.text: Check your balance to confirm no debit occurred, then block and report the UPI ID
Uninstall your banking app permanently
options.explanationWrong: Your official app is safe when you decline unknown requests.

options.text: Send ₹1 to test whether the UPI ID belongs to a business
options.explanationWrong: Never send money to test suspicious accounts.

questions.explanationCorrect: Confirm your balance is untouched and block/report the requester so they cannot send repeat prompts.
